messages:
samantha: ran a set of nsys + perfetto traces against the kernel-selector path on prod-like load. seeing intermittent 80-200ms "compile" spikes that line up with batch-size=8 incoming requests for the gpt-8k model. attaching trace links and a short dump below.

jake: can you paste the nsys commands and a quick summary of what the spike looks like in the timeline?

samantha: sure. command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,kernel -o /tmp/ksel_run \ 
  --sample=none --stats=true 
  ./benchmark_client --model gpt-8k --batch 8 --seq 2048 --qps 50
```
opened the .qdrep in Nsight and also uploaded perfetto to the trace server: https://perfetto/redwood/traces/ksel/1823456789

summary: most requests have kernel exec time ~0.8-1.6ms per token, but every ~30-120s we get a ~80-200ms blocking region where the runtime is doing JIT/compile-like work (Triton/XLA codegen path). the NVTX slices show: "compile_kernels" spans that contain a bunch of tiny CUDA kernel launches and a couple of host-side kernel compilation steps.

priya: did you check KV cache hit rates around those spikes? wonder if a KV miss pattern triggers a different kernel selection codepath.

samantha: yes — I correlated with the KV cache metric timelines. when batch size is 8, kv_cache hits drop from ~99.2% to ~70-75% for one minute windows around the spikes. looks like clients send slightly different prefix shapes that result in different cache keys, evicting the useful prefix entries and forcing the runtime to rebuild KV/KV-layout and reselect kernels.

owen: that aligns with something I instrumented last week — kernel cache key includes (model, opt-level) but NOT batch_shape or seq_len in the legacy key. so if the layout changes (e.g., varying seq_len distribution in same batch), it can fall through to compile path and insert a new kernel into the cache. we probably need to include batch_shape+seq_len (quantized buckets) in cache key.

samantha: here's the parse output of the nsys-assisted kernel timeline (abridged):

```
[time_ms] event
12012.32 kernel: forward_main (0.9ms)
12012.45 kernel: attention_kv (1.1ms)
12012.60 compile_kernels (host, 143.8ms)
12012.74 kernel: forward_main (1.0ms)
12014.00 kernel: attention_kv (1.2ms)
```

and a small table of observed compile durations from 30 runs: 
- median compile: 4.3ms (fast codegen cases)
- 95th: 148.7ms (path that triggers codegen + cuModule load)
- max: 205.1ms

jake: 95th at 148ms is huge for our latency SLO. can you see which codegen path ran? Triton cache miss vs simple kernel variant?

samantha: NVTX labels indicate "triton_codegen -> cuobjdump -> cuModuleLoad" in the big ones. small ones are just "kernel_lookup" and fast memcpy.

priya: do we have heuristics that pick smaller kernels for batch<=8? iirc we fall back to single-instance kernels for low batch sizes which are slower per-token but avoid big memory churn; maybe that logic is toggling and causing compilation work.

owen: yes the selector has a few branches:
- prefer_batched: if avg_batch>=16 -> use batched fused kernels (precompiled)
- prefer_single: if avg_batch<16 -> pick minimal-footprint kernel (sometimes requires JIT-specialization for seq_len)

when traffic oscillates around the 16 boundary, we see churn: we evict a batched kernel and then recompile when a burst pushes avg_batch above 16. but your case is batch=8 stable, so the surprising bit is the codegen happening even though prefer_single should pick an existing variant. that suggests the cache key mismatch Owen mentioned.

jake: any quick repro? if we can reproduce on a local node with a controlled client we can test fixes (cache key tweak / prewarm).

samantha: yes, repro script I used:
```bash
# reproduce pattern: alternating prefixes that cause different kv layout
python tests/repro_kernel_cache_churn.py --model gpt-8k --batch 8 --prefix-pattern alternating --duration 600
```
I can share the small trace bundle (5MB) if you want to run locally.

infra-bot: uploaded trace bundle to s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1823456789/ksel_bundle.zip :white_check_mark:

priya: propose mitigation plan: 
1) add batch_shape+seq_len_bucket to kernel cache key (low risk)
2) prewarm top-3 kernel variants at process start for models with high qps (configurable flag)
3) short-term: detect compile_kernels NVTX and return a lightweight fallback (do not block latency-critical requests)

owen: +1. also we should throttle concurrent codegen tasks — right now multiple requests can all trigger compile for the same variant and we get N x 150ms. a singleflight dedupe is needed.

jake: can we roll a canary change with key tweak + singleflight and measure? we should watch token latency p50/p95 and KV hit rate.

samantha: I'll open a PR for the cache-key patch (small). will also add singleflight guard around codegen. plan: canary on dedicated pool 3 for 24h.

priya: add observability: expose kernel_cache.hit_ratio, codegen.concurrent_count, last_codegen_duration_ms to the console so we can alert.

owen: one more note — quantization profiles can change kernel selection; make sure the cache key includes quantization backend/version. otherwise we get silent mismatches after a quantization update.

jake: ok action items:
- samantha: PR for cache key change + singleflight (ETA EOD)
- samantha: run canary and upload perfetto trace after 12h
- priya: add observability metrics (small dashboard)
- owen: review quantization key semantics and ensure it's in cache key

samantha: will do. attaching the perfetto and nsys links again: https://perfetto/redwood/traces/ksel/1823456789 and s3://redwood-traces/eng-runtime/1823456789/ksel_bundle.zip

jake: thanks — big win if we can eliminate 95th compile spikes. :100:
